did_you_know.text: Did you know? The Queen of Sheba came to Jerusalem to test Solomon with riddles after hearing about his wisdom and his devotion to the name of the Lord.
Did you know? The Queen of Sheba came to Jerusalem with a large entourage, including camels carrying spices, great quantities of gold, and precious stones.
Did you know? Solomon answered all the Queen of Sheba’s questions, and the text emphasizes that nothing was hidden from him that he could not explain to her.

Did you know? The Queen of Sheba was impressed not only by Solomon’s wisdom, but also by the food at his table, the seating of his servants, the order of his attendants, their clothing, his cupbearers, and the burnt offerings he presented at the house of the Lord.
Did you know? The Queen of Sheba connected Solomon’s kingdom with the Lord’s love for Israel and praised him for practicing justice and righteousness.
Did you know? The Queen of Sheba gave Solomon 120 talents of gold, a very large quantity of spices, and precious stones.

Did you know? The algum wood that Hiram brought from Ophir was used to make supports for the house of the Lord and the royal palace, as well as musical instruments for the singers; the text notes that no such wood had been seen until that day.
Did you know? The weight of the gold that came to Solomon in one year was 666 talents, not counting the additional revenues from merchants, kings, and the governors of the land.

Did you know? Solomon’s ivory throne was overlaid with gold. It had six steps, lions beside the armrests, and additional lions on the steps; the text says that no other kingdom had made anything like it.
Did you know? Solomon’s royal merchants brought horses from Egypt, and the chariots and horses were also sold to the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Aram.
